born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating known safe fruits immediately for efficiency, avoids known poisons, and cautiously tastes unknown fruits only when hunger justifies the risk, ensuring long-term learning without unnecessary starvation.

The code prioritizes avoiding known poison (species or trait) and uses tasting to safely expand the database of edible fruits, switching to eating only when hunger is critical or the fruit is known safe, thus balancing long-term learning with immediate survival needs.

This code prioritizes immediate consumption of known safe fruits to maximize efficiency, uses tasting only when necessary (hungry or targeted) to learn about new species, and strictly avoids known poisons, adapting to the changing environment by relying on recent history for safety decisions.

The code prioritizes safety by checking specific species history first, then uses a global harm-rate heuristic to decide whether to taste or eat unknown fruits, ensuring survival while allowing exploration.

The code prioritizes survival by aggressively avoiding known poisons and only tasting unknown fruits when hunger is sufficient to justify the risk, preferring to carry safe food to the pantry for future use unless immediate starvation threatens.

The code implements a risk-averse foraging strategy that prioritizes learning via tasting when uncertain, leverages trait-based safety matching to avoid known poisons, and balances immediate starvation risks against long-term health by carrying safe food when hunger is manageable.

The code improves survival by generalizing poison warnings from shared traits (color, shape, smell) to new fruits of the same species, while maintaining a safer hunger threshold for tasting unknown fruits unless they are the specific target.

The code improves by using smell and shape similarity to infer safety of unknown fruits based on past experiences with other species, allowing Fagi to avoid poisons and seek foods more intelligently than just species matching.
